stories.title: Academic pressure and employment anxiety are linked
stories.summary: A systematic review in Frontiers in Psychiatry suggests academic pressure and employment anxiety are mutually reinforcing stressors for university students. Mapping literature from two major repositories, researchers found these burdens operate as an intertwined dynamic rather than independent challenges for undergraduates and postgraduates throughout their academic careers.

stories.title: Climate hazards linked to digital mental health use
stories.summary: A study of 2,542 adults across four countries found that exposure to climate-related natural hazards correlates with increased use of digital mental health support. Published in BMC Public Health, the research links this usage to the psychological distress and specific stressors caused by recent environmental events.

stories.title: Psychiatrists propose family office model for the ultra-wealthy
stories.summary: Psychiatrists from the University of Zurich have introduced Family Office Psychiatry to serve individuals with over thirty million dollars in assets. The framework aims to address mental health needs for a cohort that grew to half a million people in 2025, despite their significant infrastructural resources.

stories.title: High climate anxiety reported by Ugandan students
stories.summary: A study of secondary students in Southwestern Uganda found that 88.8 percent of adolescents report climate anxiety, while 79.2 percent report anxiety regarding natural disasters. The research assessed affective responses among students aged 13 to 19, focusing on generalized worry rather than clinical psychiatric disorders.

stories.title: Patient aggression linked to nurse burnout
stories.summary: A survey of 278 psychiatric nurses in Switzerland found that patient aggression contributes to emotional exhaustion through trauma and depersonalization. The study, published in a multicenter survey, indicates this sequential mediation model accounts for 58.9 percent of the observed burnout among the nursing staff.

stories.title: Medica Foundation awards $400,000 for mental health
stories.summary: The Medica Foundation has awarded $400,000 in grants to Bemidji State University and Evergreen Youth and Family Services. The funding is part of a $3 million statewide investment in mental and chemical health, intended to help programs meet individuals within their specific community contexts.

stories.title: BetterHelp patients report harmful therapist interactions
stories.summary: An investigation by Uncloseted Media reviewed 6,000 consumer complaints and identified 80 former BetterHelp patients who reported harmful interactions with therapists. Allegations include therapists discouraging LGBTQ identities, suggesting conversion therapy, or refusing to acknowledge a patient's sexuality during sessions on the platform.

stories.title: Experts weigh in on social media bans for children
stories.summary: As countries debate social media bans, experts suggest restricting screen access is not a simple solution to cyberbullying. With 85 percent of Indian children reporting online harassment, psychiatrists note that modern abuse extends beyond physical harm, as children increasingly measure their worth through public digital metrics.

stories.title: Mindfulness program shows preliminary well-being gains
stories.summary: A community-based trial at Kyung Hee University evaluated an eight-week Mindfulness-based Vitality Promotion curriculum. The study reported high participant acceptability and preliminary improvements in psychological and physical well-being among community-dwelling adults enrolled in a lifelong learning setting, according to findings in Frontiers in Public Health.

stories.title: Exercise mindfulness linked to resilience in older adults
stories.summary: A study of 486 older adults in China identified serial indirect associations between mindfulness during exercise and positive mental health. Published in Frontiers in Public Health, the research suggests that sleep regularity and self-control serve as correlates between present-moment awareness and psychological functioning in later life.

stories.title: Mindfulness training enhances hospital staff metacognition
stories.summary: A quasi-experimental study in Discover Mental Health found that a brief mindfulness program improved metacognition and professional quality of life for hospital personnel in Pakistan. Frontline nurses reported the greatest improvements after participating in the organizational educational curriculum between February and July 2025.

stories.title: Dhaka, let’s go outside: Three days of wellness, music and mindfulness
stories.summary: In a city where traffic, deadlines and endless screen time often leave little room to breathe, Dhaka residents were invited to rediscover wellbeing beneath the open sky. The Flow Fest returned for its fifth edition with Winter Wellness, a three-day celebration from November 12 to 14 at Fortis Platinum Lounge

stories.title: Online learning linked to fewer insomnia symptoms in students
stories.summary: A study of 4,226 students in China suggests that not all screen time is equal. Researchers found that voluntary digital engagement, specifically self-directed learning, was associated with fewer insomnia symptoms. The study challenges the practice of treating all screen time as a uniform health hazard.

stories.title: Insomnia linked to higher risk of stroke and other conditions
stories.summary: A review of studies involving millions of participants found that insomnia is linked to a 26 percent increased risk of stroke. Researchers from Austria, Germany, Italy and Switzerland noted that the findings do not prove insomnia directly causes these health issues. Correlation is not causation.

stories.title: Frequent sleep starts linked to anxiety and poor sleep
stories.summary: A survey of 194 adults in Austria and Germany found that people who experience weekly sleep starts report higher levels of anxiety and worse sleep quality. Because the data was collected at a single point in time, researchers cannot determine which factor causes the other.

stories.title: Sleep apnea common in older adults with type 1 diabetes
stories.summary: A study published in Diabetes Care reports a high prevalence of poor sleep quality and obstructive sleep apnea among older adults with type 1 diabetes. Researchers identified long-term glycemic exposure and microvascular complications as risk factors, suggesting sleep health should be part of comprehensive diabetes management.

stories.title: Eczema linked to sleep problems in children
stories.summary: A review of 26,000 health records found that 12 percent of children with eczema experienced sleep problems, compared to 10 percent of children without the condition. The study confirms an association between atopic dermatitis and sleep disturbance in patients from birth to age 21.

stories.title: Alaska sleep clinic expands with virtual care
stories.summary: Quiet Sky Sleep Clinic has begun offering virtual appointments to patients across Alaska. The clinic, founded by nurse practitioner Esther Heath-Mills, plans to introduce in-person visits in Juneau starting February 1, 2027. Virtual care is now reaching the Last Frontier.

stories.title: Poor sleep linked to delirium risk after stroke
stories.summary: A study of older adults hospitalized with acute ischemic stroke found that poor sleep quality on the previous night was associated with a higher risk of subsyndromal delirium. Researchers suggest that tracking self-reported sleep parameters may help clinicians monitor cognitive status during post-stroke care.

stories.title: Physical activity linked to cognitive lapses in older adults
stories.summary: A study of community-dwelling older adults in Iran found that lower levels of physical activity are independently associated with more frequent subjective cognitive failures. Among the factors measured, including sleep quality and age, physical activity was the only one linked to self-reported cognitive lapses.

stories.summary: Skip the post-Diwali crash diet to shed weight you have gained, instead, learn how to lose weight sustainably without resorting to measures that can backfire. Celebrating with snacks, sweets, and elaborate feasts is part of the festival season, from kaju katli and gulab jamun to exquisite lunch spreads. But once

stories.title: Flywheel Squat and Leg Press Show Similar Quadriceps Activation in
stories.summary: A randomized crossover trial investigating resistance exercise mechanics has revealed that whole-repetition quadriceps muscle activation does not significantly differ between the flywheel squat and the traditional leg press in resistance-trained men. When evaluating the electrical activity of the quadriceps femoris across complete exercise repetitions, researchers identified no statistically significant differences

stories.title: Four-minute daily workout linked to strength gains
stories.summary: A 12-week trial at Penn State College of Medicine found that a four-minute daily routine, known as FAST-2, increased muscle strength in inactive adults over 65. The program consists of four 30-second exercises with 30-second rest intervals. Even short workouts can produce measurable results.

stories.title: 5 Exercises That Can Strengthen Your Quads Besides Squats - Health.com
Texas A&M studies firefighter health
stories.summary: Texas A&M researchers are tracking 115 Frisco firefighters to determine how 24-hour shift schedules affect health indicators like sleep quality and heart rate. The yearlong study monitors participants through wearable health trackers during their active duty and recovery periods. The data aims to quantify the physiological toll of emergency work.

stories.title: MIND diet shows limited link to PMS
stories.summary: A study of 405 women found that adherence to the MIND diet had a weak inverse association with premenstrual syndrome severity. The research, conducted by teams in Türkiye, concluded that the diet failed to serve as an independent predictor of symptom intensity in the adult participants.

stories.title: Dietary balance linked to lower frailty risk
stories.summary: A study of 23,673 Chinese adults found that higher diet balance scores were associated with a lower risk of accumulating health deficits. Participants with high scores saw a 36 percent lower risk of crossing frailty thresholds. Dietary insufficiency emerged as a notable risk factor for long-term health decline.

stories.title: Fiber supplement tested for IBS relief
stories.summary: Researchers at Edith Cowan University tested a fiber blend called ur gut on patients with irritable bowel syndrome. The team reported improved gut health and reduced gut-related anxiety without worsening common symptoms like bloating or pain. The supplement is intended to offer a new management strategy for IBS patients.

stories.title: Fiber blend shows promise for IBS
stories.summary: Scientists at Edith Cowan University have developed a fiber supplement designed to improve gut health in people with irritable bowel syndrome. The blend reportedly avoids worsening digestive symptoms while potentially reducing gut-related anxiety. Researchers noted rapid changes in gut bacteria during the testing of the specially designed formula.

stories.title: Coffee consumption linked to digestive changes
stories.summary: A University of Copenhagen study using electronic capsules to monitor the digestive tract found that habitual coffee drinking may alter bowel movements and colon contractions. The research also connected regular coffee intake to a richer variety of gut bacteria. The device captured internal conditions as it progressed through participants.

stories.title: Probiotics stabilize gut health during travel
stories.summary: A randomized trial of 40 healthy travelers found that a two-strain probiotic formulation preserved gut microbiota diversity during long-haul trips. While placebo recipients experienced significant depletion of microbial richness, those taking probiotics maintained stable levels. The stabilization was associated with fewer reports of gastrointestinal distress during the seven-day journey.

stories.title: Review finds goat milk formula lacks clinical proof
stories.summary: A narrative review of 172 publications concluded that while goat milk-based infant formula is nutritionally adequate and safe, controlled trials do not establish it as a treatment for gastrointestinal symptoms. Bovine milk remains the conventional standard, with goat milk formula serving as an alternative base for non-breastfed infants.

stories.title: Keto diet effects vary by fat source
stories.summary: New research in Science Advances suggests that not all ketogenic diets produce identical health outcomes. The study indicates that the specific types of fats consumed may influence inflammation and mitochondrial stress. Scientists are investigating these mechanisms to better understand the diet beyond its traditional use in treating epilepsy.

stories.title: Indian diet and walking aid diabetes remission
stories.summary: A six-month study of 87 adults found that a traditional Indian diet and daily walking helped 60.9 percent of early Type 2 diabetes patients achieve remission. The intervention used a local healthy moderate carbohydrate diet. Participants had been diagnosed with the condition within the previous two years.

stories.title: Weight management in older adults
stories.summary: Researchers suggest that many older adults may not need to lose weight, even as obesity drugs gain popularity. While some individuals pursue intermittent fasting or rigorous exercise to shed post-menopause weight, experts note that maintaining a slightly higher weight can offer benefits for the aging population.

stories.title: 4 Emerging Longevity Supplements Your Patients May Be Talking About - Verywell Health
Brain signals may predict Alzheimer's
stories.summary: Stanford researchers have identified patterns of brain activity that may predict Alzheimer's risk years before memory problems appear. These signals could offer an earlier warning than traditional biomarkers. The patterns also highlight brains that show resistance to aging, potentially informing future efforts to protect memory and cognitive function.

stories.title: Longevity testing at Super Age Games
stories.summary: The inaugural Super Age Games in New York City tested 500 amateur athletes on physical traits including agility, aerobic fitness, and balance. Participants ranging from their 20s to their 80s completed eight trials designed to measure how well they are aging. The event provided scores intended to reflect biological age.

stories.title: Exercise support linked to cancer survival
stories.summary: The international CHALLENGE trial suggests that structured, personalized exercise support can provide survival benefits for patients with colon or rectal cancer. The study indicates that the key to longevity for survivors lies in the professional guidance that sustains physical activity over time, rather than just movement alone.

stories.title: Blood sugar management for healthy aging
stories.summary: World Diabetes Day 2026 highlights the role of blood sugar regulation in metabolic health and longevity. Experts suggest that glucose management is an essential component of wellness routines beyond diabetes prevention. Maintaining stable blood sugar levels is increasingly viewed as a key factor in staying active while growing older.

stories.title: Yale study evaluates anti-aging treatments
stories.summary: Yale researchers analyzed 51 studies and found that certain prescription drugs, diets, and exercise may measurably slow biological aging. Popular anti-aging supplements appeared largely ineffective in the analysis. Whether these biological changes translate into an extended human life span remains uncertain, according to the research team.

stories.title: GLP-1s linked to increased life span in mice
stories.summary: A study found that semaglutide, a GLP-1 medication used for diabetes and obesity, extended the life span of mice by 12 percent. These findings contribute to research suggesting the drugs may slow the root cause of aging. The study raises questions about whether health should be measured by life span.

stories.title: Exercise training for seniors
stories.summary: Researchers at IHMC suggest that three days a week of combined endurance and resistance training may reduce all-cause mortality risk by up to 39 percent for people in their sixties. The study aims to address the spike in mortality risk associated with aging and frailty.

stories.title: Music therapy as a clinical practice
stories.summary: Music therapy is a structured, evidence-based healthcare profession using music to support physical, emotional, cognitive, and social wellbeing. It involves a purposeful therapeutic relationship with clear goals, assessment, and review. The practice relies on music activating multiple brain areas simultaneously to influence emotion, memory, and movement.

stories.title: Acupuncture and brain stimulation for Parkinson's
stories.summary: A study in npj Parkinson’s Disease indicates that combining subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation with acupuncture may offer complementary neurological benefits. Researchers explored whether concurrent delivery of both interventions could address psychiatric symptoms like anxiety, which remain variable when using deep brain stimulation alone.

stories.title: Mindfulness and tai chi for cancer survivors
stories.summary: The MATCH study of over 500 cancer survivors found that mindfulness and tai chi interventions were associated with reduced pain, fatigue, and sleep problems. Published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, the research involved collaboration between institutions in Canada and the United States to address long-term side effects.

stories.title: Acupuncture and rehabilitation for post-stroke swallowing
stories.summary: A network meta-analysis of 34 randomized controlled trials suggests that combining acupuncture with rehabilitation training may improve swallowing function and reduce aspiration risk in patients with post-stroke dysphagia. The review was conducted by researchers at the Second Affiliated Hospital at Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine.

stories.title: World Diabetes Day awareness
stories.summary: World Diabetes Day is observed annually on 14 November to promote prevention, early detection, and management of the condition. Launched by the International Diabetes Federation and the World Health Organization in 1991, the day was officially recognized by the United Nations in 2006.

stories.title: Dissolvable strips enter the supplement market
stories.summary: Dissolvable oral strips are emerging as a new form factor in the $79 billion supplement category, promising faster absorption and frictionless delivery. Startups like Sleep or Die and NuStrips are targeting sleep and cognitive function, with some brands securing venture funding and retail placement in lifestyle stores.

stories.title: Government efforts to promote Ayurveda
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently highlighted India's initiatives to promote traditional medicine systems, including Ayurveda, during the Golden Jubilee of a yoga research centre in Bengaluru. He noted the growing global acceptance of yoga, citing its adoption as a sport in various countries.

research.summary: Scientists have developed a promising new fiber supplement that improves gut health in people with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) without worsening bloating, pain, or other digestive symptoms. The specially designed blend also improved gut-related anxiety and produced surprisingly rapid changes in gut bacteria, potentially offering a new way.

research.title: Forcing yourself to smile can actually make you miserable
research.summary: Smiling may not always make you happier, and new research suggests that forcing yourself to smile repeatedly could actually make you feel worse. In a University of Florida study involving more than 1,100 participants, researchers discovered that while a single artificial smile can provide a small mood boost.

research.title: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression
research.summary: A simple change to your daily routine could make a surprising difference in how you feel, both physically and mentally. University of Missouri researchers found that older adults who followed consistent daily schedules reported less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression, even when they struggled with insomnia.
